title: Pointwise compact bounded coherent diagrams are compact in their functor category
statement:
Use the universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$, $\kappa$-smallness, $\kappa$-filteredness and $\kappa$-compactness of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], coherent functor categories, mapping spaces and colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and pointwise functor-category colimits of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. Let $\kappa\in\mathcal U$ be an infinite regular cardinal, let $\mathcal C$ be a locally small quasicategory fitting in $\mathcal U'$ and admitting all small $\kappa$-filtered colimits, and let $K$ be a $\kappa$-small simplicial set. If $a:K\to\mathcal C$ has $\kappa$-compact value at every vertex, then $a$ is a $\kappa$-compact object of $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$. Explicitly, for every small $\kappa$-filtered quasicategory $I$, coherent diagram $D:I\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$ and colimiting coherent cocone $D\to\Delta_I b$, the cocone
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)}(a,D(-))\longrightarrow\Delta_I\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)}(a,b)$$
obtained by postcomposition with that cocone is colimiting in $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'}$. The target diagrams $D(i)$ and $b$ are arbitrary and need not be constant on $K$. The case $K=\varnothing$ is included.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.4.13, printed pp.399-401 (PDF pp.416-418), with Definition 5.3.4.5, printed p.396, and pointwise colimits Corollary 5.1.2.3, printed p.319. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical theorem.

proof.text: Put $H=\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$. The coherent functor construction in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] makes $H$ a quasicategory, and [lem-coef-functor-spine-tower-mapping-descent] gives its local smallness and identifies mapping spaces with the coherent restriction limits used below. Let $I$ be a small $\kappa$-filtered quasicategory and let $D:I\to H$ have a colimiting cocone with apex $b$. Since $\mathcal C$ has the required filtered colimits, [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] computes this cocone objectwise: for every vertex $v$ of $K$, the cocone $D(i)(v)\to b(v)$ is colimiting in $\mathcal C$. We will compare the mapping-space cocone for $a$ with these vertexwise colimits.

For a standard simplex $\Delta^n$, prove by induction on $n$ that a diagram $a:\Delta^n\to\mathcal C$ whose vertex values are $\kappa$-compact has mapping space out of $a$ commuting with the given $I$-colimit. The case $n=0$ is the vertex compactness hypothesis. For $n=1$, [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-morphism-square] identifies the mapping space with a homotopy pullback of the two endpoint mapping spaces over the intervening mapping space; [lem-coef-spaces-kappa-limit-filtered-colimit] interchanges this finite homotopy limit with the $I$-colimit, and naturality identifies the resulting comparison with postcomposition by the given cocone. For $n>1$, let $S_0=\Delta^{\{0\}}$ and, for $0\leq j<n$, let $S_{j+1}$ be the union of the first $j+1$ consecutive spine edges and their vertices. The spine equivalence in [lem-coef-functor-spine-tower-mapping-descent] identifies mapping spaces for $a$ with those for $a|_{S_n}=a|_{\operatorname{Sp}[n]}$. For each $j$, $S_{j+1}=S_j\amalg_{\Delta^{\{j\}}}\Delta^{\{j,j+1\}}$, where the vertex inclusion is degreewise injective; [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-excision] therefore expresses the mapping space for $S_{j+1}$ as a homotopy pullback of the spaces for $S_j$ and that edge over the common vertex. Induction on $j$, the already proved $n=1$ case for the edge, and the spaces lemma give the filtered-colimit comparison at every stage. Thus the comparison from the colimit of the mapping-space diagram to the mapping space into $b$ is an equivalence, including its coherent cocone maps.

For $m\geq-1$ let $P(m)$ be the claim: for every $\kappa$-small simplicial set $L$ of dimension at most $m$ (all nondegenerate simplices of dimension $\leq m$; dimension $-1$ means $L=\varnothing$) and every $a:L\to\mathcal C$ with $\kappa$-compact vertex values, $a$ is $\kappa$-compact in $\operatorname{Fun}(L,\mathcal C)$ in the explicit sense of the statement, with the actual postcomposition cocone maps. By Step 1 the restriction of the given colimiting cocone along any map $L'\to K$, in particular along a skeleton or along a simplex $\Delta^n\to K$, is again colimiting, so $P(m)$ may be applied to these restrictions. Base $P(-1)$: $\operatorname{Fun}(\varnothing,\mathcal C)=\Delta^0$ by the defining formula, every mapping space is terminal, and the empty-shape clause of [lem-coef-spaces-kappa-limit-filtered-colimit] shows that the $I$-colimit of terminal spaces is terminal. Inductive step $P(n-1)\Rightarrow P(n)$ for $n\geq0$: let $L$ have dimension at most $n$, so $L=L_n$, writing $L_k=\operatorname{sk}_kL$. Write $A_n=\coprod_{\sigma\in(L_n)^{\mathrm{nd}}}\partial\Delta^n$ and $E_n=\coprod_{\sigma\in(L_n)^{\mathrm{nd}}}\Delta^n$, the coproducts over the nondegenerate $n$-simplices of $L$, with the attaching map $A_n\to L_{n-1}$ and the boundary inclusion $A_n\hookrightarrow E_n$ ($\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$). The decomposition of simplices in [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition] gives the degreewise pushout $L_n\cong L_{n-1}\amalg_{A_n}E_n$: a simplex of $L_n$ not in $L_{n-1}$ is uniquely a degeneracy of a unique nondegenerate $n$-simplex, and a simplex of $\Delta^n$ not in $\partial\Delta^n$ is uniquely a degeneracy of the top simplex. The map $A_n\hookrightarrow E_n$ is degreewise injective, so it is the injective leg required by [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-excision]. The defining formula for coherent functors gives $\operatorname{Fun}(E_n,\mathcal C)=\prod_\sigma\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^n,\mathcal C)$ and likewise for $A_n$, and the right-pinched mapping spaces of a product are the products of the mapping spaces; so the mapping space on $E_n$ (and on $A_n$) is the product of the mapping spaces on its cells (and their boundaries). Each cell is covered by Step 2; each boundary $\partial\Delta^n$ and $L_{n-1}$ have dimension at most $n-1$ and are $\kappa$-small, so they are covered by $P(n-1)$; and there are fewer than $\kappa$ cells because $L$ is $\kappa$-small. Mapping excision expresses the mapping space on $L_n$ as the corresponding homotopy pullback, naturally in the target diagram, while [lem-coef-spaces-kappa-limit-filtered-colimit] commutes both the products of fewer than $\kappa$ factors (a discrete $\kappa$-small shape) and the pullback (the finite shape $\Lambda^2_2$) with the $I$-colimit. This proves $P(n)$. Hence $P(m)$ holds for all $m$: every finite-dimensional $\kappa$-small $L$ with pointwise $\kappa$-compact values is $\kappa$-compact in $\operatorname{Fun}(L,\mathcal C)$, with the actual postcomposition cocone maps.

For arbitrary $K$, write $K=\bigcup_{n\ge0}\operatorname{sk}_nK$. If $\kappa=\aleph_0$, then $K$ has only finitely many nondegenerate simplices, hence bounded dimension, so it is one of the finite-dimensional cases of Step 3. If $\kappa>\aleph_0$, the indexing nerve $N(\mathbb N^{\mathrm{op}})$ is $\kappa$-small. The tower clause of [lem-coef-functor-spine-tower-mapping-descent] identifies the mapping space out of $a$ with the homotopy limit of the mapping spaces out of its skeleta. Each skeleton comparison is an equivalence by Step 3, and [lem-coef-spaces-kappa-limit-filtered-colimit] interchanges this $\kappa$-small homotopy limit with the $I$-filtered colimit. Hence the comparison cocone for $a$ is colimiting. If $K=\varnothing$, the defining formula gives $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)=\Delta^0$ and all relevant mapping spaces are terminal; their filtered colimit is terminal by the empty-shape clause of the same spaces lemma.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NJ-40da1dba7 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, its four steps and the statements of all eight cited nodes. The source is HTT Prop. 5.3.4.13 (not archived; the worker's WANTED line stands). The statement matches the source hypothesis by hypothesis: kappa regular in U, C locally small with small kappa-filtered colimits, K kappa-small, vertexwise kappa-compact values, arbitrary non-constant targets, actual postcomposition cocone, and K empty included. Nothing is weakened. There are no new nodes, no cycle (checked over the 427-node closure), and no departure from the unit route: five cited statements are in sk-prop-sf-biduality-general, the other two are a definition and a Mathlib leaf, so tool_uses [] is correct. No SGA is cited. lem-coef-accessible-diagram-presentations states the same compactness only as a special case under accessibility hypotheses, so it is not a duplicate. Step 1: the Yoneda/presheaf-limits lemma gives the vertexwise (and restricted) colimit cocones, and the spine-tower lemma gives local smallness. Step 2: the arrow mapping square plus the finite-limit interchange handles Delta^1, and the spine equivalence with excision along injective vertex legs handles Delta^n. Step 3: the skeletal pushout follows from the nondegenerate decomposition, Fun of a coproduct is a product of fewer than kappa factors, and excision applies. Step 4: kappa = aleph_0 gives finite dimension; for uncountable kappa the tower clause and interchange over N(N^op), which is kappa-small, finish the proof; K empty is the terminal case. Small cases checked: Delta^0, an arrow of finite sets, K empty, and an infinite discrete K, which shows the kappa-smallness hypothesis is needed. One D4 fault repaired: Step 3's induction had no stated claim or base case and applied the 'induction hypothesis' to the boundaries of Delta^n. The fix rewrites only Step 3's text: it states P(m) for all kappa-small L of dimension at most m, the base P(-1) via the empty-shape clause, and the step from P(n-1) to P(n). uses and proof_deps are unchanged. Universe re-indexing from S_U to S_{U'} for the spaces lemma is accepted as standard.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
